channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: PM Netanyahu congratulates Israeli men's marathon team European Athletics Championships gold
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu congratulated the Israeli men's marathon team on their historic win of the team gold medal at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.
"Our athletes displayed extraordinary determination, dedication, and teamwork, bringing immense honor and a great source of national pride to the State of Israel. Well done!" the Prime Minister proclaimed.

item.title: New Haredi party could shake up Shas and UTJ
item.description: A haredi politician met with senior rabbis opposed to IDF conscription, as part of talks to establish a new party aimed at restoring the deferment for yeshiva students.

item.title: Everything is computerized, so why do elections rely on paper ballots?
item.description: Shutting down the economy on Election Day costs the Israeli economy between two and three billion shekels. So why not save billions and vote from home? Prof. Orr Dunkelman explains why the traditional ballot box is still preferable.

item.title: MK reveals his demands for the next Israeli government
item.description: MK Simcha Rothman tells Arutz Sheva he wants to continue judicial reform, overhaul the attorney general's powers and help shape the next right-wing government.

item.title: Recovery after the Iran War: GDP jumps 15.4%
item.description: The Central Bureau of Statistics publishes a preliminary estimate according to which GDP jumped in the second quarter of 2026 by 15.4% on an annualized basis, which is 3.6% compared to the previous quarter. The figure reflects a sharp recovery from the war against Iran, but may still be updated.

item.title: Children ate chocolate on vacation and began hallucinating
item.description: Two children, ages five and six, were exposed during a family vacation to chocolate containing hallucinogenic mushrooms and hospitalized.

item.title: Hundreds of students visit Rabbi Kook’s gravesite
item.description: Students from the Beit El Yeshiva, together with Rosh Yeshiva Rabbi Zalman Baruch Melamed and the yeshiva’s rabbis, gathered to pray at the gravesite of Rabbi Abraham Isaac Kook.

item.title: 'This time we won't stop:' Coalition chairman's vow on judicial reform
item.description: Coalition chairman Ofir Katz declares that if Likud forms the next government, the judicial reform will return to the Knesset agenda.

item.title: Ben-Gvir: 8 top Likud figures asked to join Otzma Yehudit
item.description: Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir says four Likud ministers and four MKs approached him about joining Otzma Yehudit in light of its rising poll numbers.

item.title: What Jason Arday teaches us About Israel’s predicament
item.description: The interesting question is not simply how Arday behaved. It is how institutions behaved around him. And how the pattern fits the post October 7th mendacity. Opinion.

item.title: Hamas: Meetings in Egypt are intended to advance the roadmap for a ceasefire
item.description: Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem claims that the meetings in Egypt were intended to update the mediators on "Israeli violations" and advance the roadmap.

item.title: Following the Bondi Beach attack: Australia will buy back weapons from civilians
item.description:
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced today that the state of New South Wales will launch a program to purchase weapons from citizens.
The program is part of the national response to the Bondi Beach shooting attack last year in which 15 people were murdered at a Hanukkah event.

item.title: Live: Memorial for Rabbi Kook in Jerusalem
item.description: Today, on Tuesday, 3 Elul, a memorial for Rabbi Avraham Yitzhak HaKohen Kook is held at the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem and is broadcast live to the general public.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister: No intention of returning to negotiations with US
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that "60 days have passed since the agreement signed with the US, we have no intention at the moment to return to negotiations with the United States."

item.title: Israeli arrested in Greece: Barbecue sparks wildfire
item.description: The 35-year-old tourist is suspected of lighting a barbecue at a vacation villa despite an explicit ban.

item.title: Our war today
item.description: Chazon Ish: “It appears that what we learned in the Mishnah, that in an obligatory war even a groom goes out from his chamber, does not refer to a situation in which their assistance is needed to win the war, for it is obvious that for the sake of saving lives and saving the nation, everyone is obligated."

item.description: Jared Kushner once claimed he read 25 books on the Israel-Palestine conflict, defending his role as an ‘expert’ forging the Trump administration's Middle East peace plan. We can relax now. Op-ed.

item.title: Israeli universities rank among world’s top 100
item.description: Two Israeli research institutions have earned places among the world’s 100 leading universities in the 2026 Shanghai ranking, with Weizmann retaining 71st place and Hebrew University ranking 89th.

item.title: Hezbollah terrorist eliminated: Wave of strikes in Lebanon after soldiers' injuries
item.description: The IDF carried out strikes overnight Sunday in the Ali Taher Ridge area of Lebanon, while also eliminating terrorist Abu Hassan Alaa, a senior commander in Hezbollah's Badr Unit.

item.title: Ukrainian drones hit Russian retail giant site near Moscow
item.description: Ukrainian drones last night struck the huge logistics complex of the Russian retail giant WildBreeze in the village of Koldino in the Podolsk region, south of Moscow.

item.title: Iran executed man covicted of running over police during protest
item.description:
Iran announced that it has executed Shahram Sadeghi, who was convicted of running over seven police officers during a wave of anti-regime protests. The execution was carried out following a ruling by a court in the city of Karaj.
The Iranian court convicted Sadeqi on serious charges of "operational activity in favor of the Zionist regime, the United States, and hostile groups."

item.title: Suspected grenade thrown in Tel Aviv, causing explosion
item.description:
The police have opened an investigation into a suspected grenade attack in south Tel Aviv after receiving a report of hearing an explosion near a residential building in the Kiryat Shalom neighborhood.
The police statement stated that damage was caused at the scene and that police and a bomb disposal squad arrived at the scene and began investigating and collecting evidence. The background is believed to be a criminal incident.

item.title: State Department Spokesperson: Hezbollah is the main obstacle to Lebanon's economic recovery
item.description:
A spokesman for the US State Department said in an interview with Al Jazeera that Hezbollah is the main obstacle to Lebanon's economic reconstruction and growth.
According to the spokesman, the terrorist organization "bears sole responsibility for the Israeli presence on the territory of the country." He further emphasized Washington's position regarding the continuation of the necessary steps: "The pilot areas are the only practical path to achieving peace. We expect the Lebanese army to complete the cleanup operations in these areas."

item.title: Intra-Muslim carnage dwarfs the Israel-Palestinian Arab conflict
item.description: The immensity of the intra-Muslim carnage dwarfs the regional and global significance of the Arab-Israeli conflict and the Palestinian Arab issue. Op-ed.
